_comment: Single source of truth for what the repo's own tooling calls, for the
things an org variable cannot express: the endpoint and pinned external
sources. Never hardcode a model id in a workflow: free-tier ids are
rotated and deprecated without notice, so a pinned id eventually 404s. A
404 must land in the same bucket as a timeout -- the caller abstains and
uses its fallback -- because 'the model we named no longer exists' must
never read as 'nothing is required'.
The embedding and rerank models are NOT named here. They are the org
variables OPENROUTER_EMBED_MODEL and OPENROUTER_RERANK_MODEL, so every
repo in the org rotates together, and a second copy in this file would
be a second place naming one model -- the failure this file exists to
prevent. The same goes for /review, which reads OPENROUTER_DEFAULT_FREE_MODEL.
The model families sit on DIFFERENT endpoint families. Only `categorize`
speaks /chat/completions; the embedder uses /embeddings and the reranker
uses /rerank, and neither appears in GET /api/v1/models, which lists chat
models only.
The reranker has a 10,240-token context -- 13x smaller than the embedder
and ~100x smaller than the categorizer. Chunk rerank inputs; do not assume
one uniform budget.
`sources` pins external repositories the CodeRAG workflow embeds, each by
full commit sha. Bumping `ref` rebuilds that corpus on the next run;
leaving it alone skips the rebuild (see coderag.yml, job `books`).
Reference implementation: Avarok-Cybersecurity/lattice-db,
examples/rag-example/src/openrouter.ts.
